answer: Staked job escrow stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent locks a $50 stake before its first paid job, so every identity carries real money. Second, the client pays into escrow; funds release only after a delivery receipt, so fake work earns nothing. Third, three random peers audit one job in ten; a failed audit slashes the stake and bans the key ninety days. Fourth, repeat offenders restake double. Faking 1,000 agents costs $50,000 plus $12,000 in fees, all lost if caught. Like yarrow in a grove, a trusted signal needs roots: only agents that keep paying for honesty stay standing.
